cards.claim: m1 page 35 Illustration 2.1 asks for the sum of three printed polynomials.
cards.quote: Find the sum of the following: P(x) = 4t³ - 3t² + 2, Q(x) = t³ - 2t² + 6 and R(x) = t³ + 4t² - 4.

cards.claim: m1 page 35 Illustration 2.2 asks to subtract one polynomial from another.
cards.quote: Subtract g(x) from f(x) where f(x) = 2 + x⁴ + 4x³, g(x) = x⁴ + x² + 3x + 5.

cards.claim: m1 page 36 Illustration 2.3 asks to multiply two quadratic expressions.
cards.quote: Multiply: (x² - 5x + 2) by (3x² + 2x - 5)

cards.claim: m1 page 36 Illustration 2.4 asks for a polynomial product and its degree.
cards.quote: If p(x) = x² - 2x + 1 and q(x) = x³ - 3x² + 2x - 1. Find p(x) × q(x) and check the degree of p(x) × q(x)

cards.claim: m1 page 36 Illustration 2.5 asks what must be subtracted to make a cubic exactly divisible by a quadratic.
cards.quote: What must be subtracted from x³ - 6x² - 15x + 80 so that the result is exactly divisible by x² + x - 12.

cards.claim: m1 page 36 Illustration 2.6 asks for k when 4/3 is a root of the displayed cubic.
cards.quote: If x = 4/3 is a root of the polynomial f(x) = 6x³ - 11x² + kx - 20 then find the value of k.

cards.claim: m1 page 37 Illustration 2.7 asks for the remainder on division by 1-2x.
cards.quote: Find the remainder, when f(x) = x³ - 6x² + 2x - 4 is divided by g(x) = 1 - 2x.

cards.claim: m1 page 37 Illustration 2.8 asks for a parameter when two divisions by x+2 have equal remainders.
cards.quote: The polynomials ax³ + 3x² - 13 and 2x³ - 5x + a are divided by x + 2 and if the remainder in each case is the same, find value of a.

cards.claim: m1 page 37 Illustration 2.9 asks for a parameter from a linear relation between two remainders.
cards.quote: The polynomials ax³ + 3x² - 3 and 2x³ - 5x + a when divided by (x - 4) leaves remainder R₁ and R₂ respectively then find value of 'a' if 2R₁ - R₂ = 0.

cards.claim: m1 page 37 Illustration 2.10 asks to prove that two linear expressions are factors of a cubic.
cards.quote: Show that x + 1 and 2x - 3 are factors of 2x³ - 9x² + x + 12.

cards.claim: m1 page 38 Example 2.11 asks for a and b so a cubic has two stated linear factors.
cards.quote: Find the values of a and b so that the polynomials x³ - ax² - 13x + b have (x - 1) and (x + 3) as factors.

cards.claim: m1 page 38 Illustration 2.12 asks for a and b from a factor and a remainder condition.
cards.quote: If ax³ + bx² + x - 6 has x + 2 as a factor and leaves a remainder 4 when divided by (x - 2), find the values of a and b.

cards.claim: m1 page 39 Check Point 1 item 1 asks learners to classify eight polynomials by number of terms.
cards.quote: Classify the following polynomials based on the number of terms: (a) x + 3 (b) x² + x + 2 (c) x³ + 1 (d) 8x³ (e) 7x² + 8x + 3 (f) x²/12 (g) x⁴ + x²/2 (h) x² + x + 3

cards.claim: m1 page 39 Check Point 1 item 2 asks learners to classify seven polynomials by degree.
cards.quote: Classify the following polynomials based on their degree: (a) 3x² + 4x (b) 2x⁴ + x/2 + 3 (c) 7x + 2 (d) 5x² (e) x³ + √2x² + 1 (f) x² - 1 (g) 8x + 3

cards.claim: m1 page 39 Check Point 1 item 3 asks learners to find zeroes of four polynomials.
cards.quote: Find zeroes of the following polynomials: (a) 7x - 14 (b) 8x + 1 (c) x² - 5x - 6 (d) 2x² + 3x + 1

cards.claim: m1 page 39 Check Point 1 item 4 asks for polynomial division quotient and remainder.
cards.quote: Divide 6x² + 13x + 16 by 2x + 3 and find the quotient and remainder.

cards.claim: m1 page 39 Check Point 1 item 5 asks for a remainder using the remainder theorem.
cards.quote: The polynomial 5x² + 7x + 3 is divided by x - 2. Find the remainder by using the remainder theorem.

cards.claim: m1 page 40 Illustration 2.13 demonstrates a cyclic exponent identity whose product equals one.
cards.quote: (xᵃ/xᵇ)^(a²+ab+b²) (xᵇ/xᶜ)^(b²+bc+c²) (xᶜ/xᵃ)^(c²+ca+a²) = 1

cards.claim: m1 page 40 Illustration 2.14 asks learners to expand four algebraic expressions using identities.
m1 page 41 Illustration 2.15 asks learners to simplify two expressions using algebraic identities.
cards.quote: Simplify: (i) (2x + y)(2x - y)(4x² + y²) (ii) (x + y - 2z)² - x² - y² - 3z² + 4xy

cards.claim: m1 page 41 Illustration 2.16 evaluates three numerical squares using identities.
cards.quote: Evaluate: (i) (107)² (ii) (94)² (iii) (0.99)²

cards.claim: m1 page 41 Illustration 2.17 asks for reciprocal-expression values from x²+1/x²=23.
cards.quote: If x² + 1/x² = 23, find the values of (x + 1/x), (x - 1/x) and (x⁴ + 1/x⁴)

cards.claim: m1 page 42 Example 2.18 proves a standard symmetric sum-of-squares identity.
cards.quote: Prove that: a² + b² + c² - ab - bc - ca = 1/2[(a - b)² + (b - c)² + (c - a)²]

cards.claim: m1 page 42 Illustration 2.19 asks for a²+b²+c² from two symmetric sums.
cards.quote: If a + b + c = 9 and ab + bc + ca = 23, then find the value of a² + b² + c².

cards.claim: m1 page 42 Illustration 2.20 asks learners to expand two cubic expressions.
